contexts.text: A measure of wheat for a penny = that love is so rare; three measures of barley for a penny = that charity is so.

A measure of wheat for a penny, and three measures of barley for a penny () = because the estimation of good and truth is so little, that it is scarcely any. These things are signified, because by a measure, which was both a measure and the quantity measured, is signified quality.

A measure of wheat for a penny, and three measures of barley for a penny = that the genuine good of the Church with them is as nothing, and also the genuine truth of the Church; as is evident from the signification of a measure, which was the measure for wheat and barley with the Greeks, and which = the quality of the estimation; for by measures in the Word... is signified the quality of a thing as to good and as to truth.
